newsitem.title: USA: BP says cut crude, natgas output in US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: BP says cut crude, natgas output in US Gulf.

text.p: British Petroleum said Monday it cut some crude oil and natural gas production at three offshore oil platforms in the U.S. Gulf Coast due to Tropical Storm Josephine.
A total of 67,000 barrels per day (bpd) of gross crude oil and 64 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gross natural gas were reduced from three out of four fields operated by BP.
BP operates about 70,000 bpd of gross crude and 72 million mmcfd of gross natural gas in the U.S. Gulf.
The three platforms shut-in since Sunday afternoon were Pompano, Amberjack and Ewing Bank 826.
"We're expecting to send these guys back into the fields by tomorrow," said Hugh Depland, spokesman for BP Exploration.
Tropical Storm Josephine is expected to make landfall in a few hours off Florida's Gulf Coast. Winds are now about 70 miles per hour.
